subject: SynapsePay prod: unexplained 5xx and tail latency — path signal degradation
thread_content:
From: Elaine Zhou <elaine.zhou@synapsepay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: SynapsePay SRE <sre@synapsepay.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Production spike: latency + 5xx — looks like network path issues

Hi Evelyn,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx errors and a 3x increase in tail latency from our checkout traffic to your inference API starting 09:05 PT. Error rate is ~8% on p95 requests, throughput reduced by ~30% for a subset of origins (us-west-2). Our SRE team captured TCP traces and service traces attached.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (peering, proxy, DNS) in the last hour? This is impacting conversion for our merchants — we need mitigation ASAP and an executive contact if this is platform-level.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Zhou
Director, Platform Engineering | SynapsePay
attachments: tcpdumps.tar.gz, service-traces.zip

---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: SynapsePay SRE <sre@synapsepay.com>, Elaine Zhou <elaine.zhou@synapsepay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: latency + 5xx — looks like network path issues

Elaine — thanks for the rapid heads-up and the traces. I'm escalating to network and infra now. Quick note from the first-pass triage: our edge telemetry shows increased TCP retransmits and a transient spike in DNS resolution latency for the route toward synapse's us-west-2 egress. No config pushes from Redwood in the last 24 hours on the route.

I've looped in marissa (Customer Success lead), Vivek (support/ops), Rishi (network), and Jonas (infra). We'll run parallel triage:
- Rishi + Jonas: active path checks, BGP/peering health and DNS TTLs
- Vivek: customer comms and mitigation knobs (routes, burst capacity)
- Marissa: exec notification and SLA / credit options if needed

Can one of you confirm if Acme Transit (our regional transit provider) is showing any anomalies?

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
---

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: latency + 5xx — looks like network path issues

Quick update from network: we see repeated AS path changes for the prefix announced to us-west-2 that correlate with the error window (09:04–09:18). Packet captures (we grabbed a sample) show MSS clamping and occasional ICMP fragmentation responses from a hop inside Acme Transit. DNS lookups for synapse target are also intermittently resolving to an older/secondary peering IP — TTL values briefly jumped from 30s to 300s.

Hypothesis: transient route flapping at Acme Transit + one of their edge proxies rewriting TCP options (or dropping SYN-ACKs) -> caused connection resets and fallback to slower path/DNS entry, increasing tail latency and 5xx.

Action plan I'm executing now:
- Opened NETOPS-721 with Acme Transit (copied netops@acmetransit.net).
- Forced an alternative peering route for affected prefixes for 15m to drain problematic path.
- Increased edge keepalive tolerance for synapse-origin traffic.
- Requested Acme to share their edge proxy config and recent deploys.

I'll post captures and service traces to the ticket. If we still see >5% 5xx after route shift, we'll temporarily shift SynapsePay to a different egress pool and enable aggressive caching for common prefixes.

Rishi
Network Lead, Redwood Inference
attachment: tcpdumps-sample.pcap
---

From: Acme Transit NetOps <netops@acmetransit.net>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:41:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: NETOPS-721 / SynapsePay — provisional investigation

Rishi / Jonas,

Thanks for the alert. We observed a software update on our edge proxy cluster at 09:02 that introduced a regression in TCP option handling when combined with certain MSS settings; that caused SYN retransmits from some peers. We're rolling back the change in region us-west-2 and will confirm once the cluster is back to the previous version. Will share logs in 15m.

Apologies for the outage impact — we know this caused route instability.

- Acme Transit NetOps
---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Zhou <elaine.zhou@synapsepay.com>, SynapsePay SRE <sre@synapsepay.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: latency + 5xx — looks like network path issues

Elaine — thanks for the traces. We just forced traffic for your us-west-2 endpoints onto the alternate peering path and are seeing error rate drop to ~1% and p95 latency drifting back toward baseline within the last 6 minutes. Acme Transit confirmed a rollback of a proxy change.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Alternate peering active for 30m (we'll extend if stable).
- Edge keepalive tolerance increased for SynapsePay.
- Short-term caching enabled for idempotent requests at the edge to reduce backend load.

Marissa will follow up on SLA credit options; Evelyn and I will coordinate an exec-level summary for you and your leadership. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and share a post-mortem.

-Vivek
Principal Support Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: sla-impact-estimate.xlsx
---

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Zhou <elaine.zhou@synapsepay.com>, SynapsePay SRE <sre@synapsepay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: SynapsePay incident update & next steps

Elaine — following up with a concise exec summary and next steps.

What happened (summary):
- 09:02 PT on 2028-07-20 an edge proxy deploy at Acme Transit introduced TCP option handling regression and caused intermittent SYN/SYN-ACK failures for traffic between SynapsePay origins and our us-west-2 edge.
- The regression triggered AS path churn and DNS TTL anomalies which caused a subset of requests to hit degraded routes, increasing p95/p99 latency and raising 5xx rate to ~8% for ~14 minutes.

What we did (short):
- Network team forced alternate peering and adjusted keepalive tolerances; observed error rate drop to ~1% within ~6 minutes.
- Worked with Acme Transit to roll back the edge change.
- Enabled short-term caching and temporary edge-scale to reduce backend pressure.

Impact:
- Estimated lost merchant conversions: see sla-impact-estimate.xlsx.
- No customer data exposure; this was infrastructure-level.

Next steps / deliverables:
- Post-mortem with timeline + runbook updates (ETA 48 hours, owner: Rishi).
- Joint RCA with Acme Transit and SynapsePay SRE (owner: Jonas).
- Offer: one-time service credit per contract guidelines; Marissa will follow up with formal offer and options.

If you want an immediate exec call, Marissa can coordinate scheduling — otherwise we'll share the post-mortem and the joint action plan within two business days.

Apologies again for the impact; we take incidents like this seriously and will be adjusting our peering health checks and adding additional DNS sanity checks to reduce the chance of similar failures.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
